A message from our Headteacher
At Bishop Fox’s School our ethos of high standards and high expectations underpins everything that we do. We work hard to create a caring and challenging learning environment in which each individual can strive, enjoy and achieve. As the Headteacher I hold a strong belief in the power of education to change children’s lives and the right of every child to receive an excellent education.
We are dedicated to building opportunities for our students to achieve the highest academic standards, ensuring that they are known as individuals and that their unique personality, talents and interests are nurtured and developed to the full.
I was delighted with the school’s most recent Ofsted report (March 2023), which judged the school to be good. In the report, the Lead Inspector wrote many very positive comments about what it is like to attend Bishop Fox’s School including ‘this is a school where excellence is aspired to and celebrated’, ‘warm relationships’ between students and staff create a harmonious atmosphere’, and ‘there is a calm and focused atmosphere in lessons and around the school site’. The report states that there are many areas where the school performs well, including ‘a very strong culture of safeguarding’.
Bishop Fox’s School is a place for students to make new friends and to enjoy many shared experiences together. We embrace the notion that young people should enjoy and achieve in their time at school. Whilst examination results are critical to children’s future lives, so is a safe and happy environment within which they can enjoy the opportunities and experiences beyond the classroom that nurtures them to become independent learners and responsible adults.
Our academic results have seen a tremendous improvement in recent years and our positive progress places us as one of the top performing secondary schools in Somerset and within the top 20% of schools nationally. It is our responsibility to enable our students to have every opportunity to achieve their full potential and be at the forefront in shaping the world of tomorrow.
We welcome into our school community the parents/guardians of students who want to learn, experience and grow into informed, high achieving, well-rounded and delightful young people. A strong partnership between parents/guardians and the school is vital in enabling children to achieve success.
Please contact the school if at any time you would like to visit us and discover more about what we have to offer.
Ms Kerry Tonkin Headteacher

Home » The Curriculum » Humanities: Geography/History/Religion & World Beliefs
Students study History, Religion & World Beliefs and Geography as separate subjects at both Key Stages.
Increasingly we adopt an enquiry based approach to learning and compliment class based work with field visits and trips locally. Geography is unique in bridging the social sciences (human geography) with the natural sciences (physical geography). Human geography concerns the understanding of the dynamics of cultures, societies and economies, and physical geography concerns the understanding of the dynamics of physical landscapes and the environment.
Students are expected to gain knowledge and understanding so that they may form opinions and actively engage in the issues of today. Moral and ethical issues are studied from an historical and contemporary perspective. A wide range of medical, social and environmental issues are covered including the development of medical treatments and contemporary ethical issues that arise; social issues such as community cohesion, the family, political responsibility, conflict and environmental concerns. All three subjects have valuable lessons in preparing our students for the challenges of tomorrow.

Careers Education and Guidance
Careers Education is an important aspect of Bishop Fox’s School. We run a programme for Year 8 to Year 11 students supporting them to make informed decisions relating to option choices at KS4, Work Experience placements in Year 10 and choice of Post 16 destinations.
The careers department is run by a careers coordinator who provides one to one careers support guidance interviews for all students. The careers department also coordinates work experience for all Year 10 students and liaison with all Post 14, 16 and 18 education and training providers.
To view our Careers Policy, please click here.
To view our Careers Programme, please click here.
To view our Provider Access Policy, please click here. (meets full requirements of Baker Clause)
To view our Careers Plan, please click here.
Our careers information is reviewed annually.
Career Education and Guidance is measured through the Gatsby Benchmark. The eight Gatsby benchmarks of Good Career Guidance are:
1. A stable careers programme
2. Learning from career and labour market information
3. Addressing the needs of each student
4. Linking curriculum learning to careers
5. Encounters with employers and employees
6. Experiences of workplaces
7. Encounters with further and higher education
8. Personal guidance
Each term we are assessed against these 8 Benchmarks. Please click here to read our latest assessment.
Bishop Fox’s Careers Team
Mrs Louise Daniels – Deputy Headteacher and Careers Lead
Mr Summerill (MEd in CareersEducation and Guidance) provides the strategic support for careers education guidance and supports careers guidance interviews through careers sessions for Years 8, 10 and 11. He also provides support for Mr Truby with careers guidance interviews.
(Tel: 01823 289211 Email: ldaniels@bishopfoxs.co.uk)
Mr James Truby – Careers Co-ordinator and Advisor
Mr Truby co-ordinates the careers education programme and meets with students on a one-to-one basis to provide advice, guidance and information regarding their next steps and career aspirations.
All students are seen in Year 10/11 for an individual interview and students are offered guidance if required when selecting their GCSE options.
Parents / Guardians are welcome to attend their child’s careers interview but would need to contact Mr Truby to arrange a convenient time.
There are also drop in sessions available in the careers office (upstairs in the Hub) at break times for students to ask any questions or to book an appointment.
The school has a designated careers library with 3 careers computers.
For students, parents / guardians who are considering pursuing the apprenticeship route, Mr Truby is happy to help with applications or to arrange a mock interview.
Measuring Impact of our Careers Programme
We measure the impact of our careers programme in a number of ways:
Feedback from employers through work experience
Feedback from local colleges and training providers
Student Leavers Destinations 2024
2024 Intended destinations can be viewed here.
We use this feedback to develop and improve our career provision on an ongoing basis.
Bishop Fox’s and our Community
Bishop Fox’s believe it is important to be in the heart of the community and as such is an outward looking School looking for opportunities to work with and for the local community.
We work with a number of local and national organisations to help deliver a varied careers programme. These include practice interviews, careers fairs, talks, workshops, work experience and campus visits.
If you are able to assist us in any way then please contact: Jtruby@bishopfoxs.co.uk
Bishop Fox’s has strong links with our local primary schools – we run a range of different curriculum opportunities for our local schools which include:
The aim is to make the transition from primary to secondary as smooth as possible and to offer our specialist curriculum and facilities to our local primary students.
Bishop Fox’s is one of only a few local schools that offer Work Experience to all students in Year 10. Students work in a range of local settings and enjoy the opportunity to experience what the world beyond Year 11 will look like.
To view our Work Experience Policy, please click here.
Bishop Fox’s holds an annual careers fair, this is attended by students form Year 8, 10 and 11. This is part of a careers curriculum day.
We have 25 stands from a range of organisations including:
And a range of local companies
Bishop Fox’s has close links with all the local colleges. We run careers days at both Bridgwater and Taunton College, Richard Huish College, Exeter College, Cannington Campus and local 6th Form Colleges. A wide range of talks, presentations and workshops run throughout the school year. Year 9 students can also spend a week in summer school at Bridgwater and Taunton College. We also run motor vehicle, hair and beauty, construction and catering vocational course’s for Year 10 and 11 students at Level 1.
We have strong links and arrange visits to a number of local universities such as Exeter and Bristol and also have links with Oxford University. We also run the Brilliant Club where Year 9 students work with PHD students to produce a university standard report and have the opportunity to visit Russell Group universities. In recent years we have worked with Southampton and Cambridge universities.
We have a strong Business and Enterprise focus and work in partnership with the a range of local business to enhance the education of our students. The school is a member of the Chamber of Commerce and run a range of joint events with them. We run practice interviews for all of Year 11. These formal interviews are to help prepare students for post 16 destinations involves 20 adults form a range of business and college environments.
We have a proud tradition of ensuring all our students make positive transitions from Bishop Fox’s. Over 90% choose to attend Richard Huish College, or Bridgwater and Taunton College choosing a range of academic and vocational options. The remaining students choose apprenticeships or go direct in to the world of work. We are a Bronze Award holder for National Citizenship Service (NCS) whereby Bishop Fox’s students follow a national transition programme after their exams in Year 11.
EMPLOYERS INFORMATION
We are happy to support employers making contact with the school to support careers education guidance in the form of talks, visits and practice interviews.
We are also very happy to facilitate the application process for appropriate students for work based training, traineeships or apprenticeships. Please contact Mr Summerill for more details (ssummerill@bishopfoxs.co.uk).
www.careerpilot.org.uk/ is a free site that helps young people plan their future study and work. It is a great resource for young people, their parents/carers and also teachers and tutors, who are advising students about the full range of options.
The National Careers Service provides information, advice and guidance across England to help you make decisions on learning, training and work. The service offers confidential and impartial advice and is supported by qualified careers advisers. https://nationalcareersservice.direct.gov.uk/
For information on Apprenticeships, what they involve and how you can find one, follow this link: www.apprenticeships.gov.uk/
The options open to students are A levels, vocational courses or apprenticeships:
A levels are two year courses that are exam based. Please refer to www.russellgroup.ac.uk ‘Informed Choices booklet’ which gives advice about essential or useful A level subjects required for certain degrees if you are aiming to apply to one of the more prestigious universities. A levels can lead on to a degree or an apprenticeship.
Vocational courses are aimed at a particular area of work. Diplomas, T levels and BTECs are ideal for students with a vocation in mind and who have a practical and hands on learning style. These qualifications can also lead on to a degree or an apprenticeship.
Apprenticeships combine practical training in a job with study.
As an apprentice you will
You will need to find an employer who is willing to offer you an apprenticeship. You will need to register on the National Apprenticeships website, www.apprenticeships.org.uk; ask family, friends etc about who might be able to offer an apprenticeship; contact businesses to enquire if they would be likely to have an apprenticeship vacancy; apply to colleges for apprenticeships.
Traineeships are a pre-apprenticeship programme that support students who would like to be an apprentice but may lack confidence and experience and the required grades. Students attend extra tuition in classrooms, gain work experience and receive support to secure an apprenticeship.

BIENVENUS! ¡BIENVENIDOS!
Welcome to the Modern Languages Faculty
At Bishop Fox’s we pride ourselves on the quality of teaching and learning in the Language Faculty.
Language learning at Bishop Fox’s is fun! Lessons are delivered using a variety of methods – songs, games and activities, ICT, plus the more traditional skills of Listening, Speaking, Reading and Writing. All students currently study French from Year 7 and all students study both French and Spanish in Year 8, continuing if they wish, to undertake a GCSE in a language at Key Stage 4.
Our biannual study visits to France have proved very successful – last year we visited the Opal Coast with excursions to St. Omer, the WW1 battlefield site Thiépual and Parc Astérix, as well as a local goat farm, a bonbonnerie and a local bakery Boulogne-Sur-Mer.
Throughout the school year there are various language activities available to different year groups to promote a wider understanding of both language and culture. Key Stage 3 students have the opportunity to have support from staff and older students with their homework weekly in MFL Club. Key Stage 4 students have the option of speaking and writing practice with languages staff weekly after school and have the opportunity to borrow French or Spanish films to improve their Listening skills.
The AQA GCSE courses are delivered to Years 9, 10 and 11, using course books – ‘Studio’ in French and ‘Viva’ in Spanish. The four skills of Listening, Reading and Writing are assessed by way of terminal exams and Oral exams in Year 11.

Our Statement of Intent
Bishop Fox’s School acknowledges that young carers may need extra support to ensure they have equal access to education. Through our Young Carer Agreement, the school sends a clear message that young carers’ education is vital. We are committed to identifying young carers early, monitoring their progress and attendance, and providing a person-centred, confidential environment where they can thrive.
Download the Full Policy
Students can be young carers for lots of different reasons:
Some young carers might be doing lots of caring, others just a small amount but are impacted by the situation at home. This can be anything, for example worrying about the person with the health condition or needing to do more things for themselves compared to other students.
There is lots of support available for young carers and their families should they ever need it – both inside and outside of school. At school you can contact Miss Adams (Young Carer Lead) or Ms Lisa Hayes (SLT Lead) via the school office: 01823 289 211 or by email: office@bishopfoxs.co.uk
You can find out more information about by visiting Somerset’s Local Offer for young carers. You can also find resources and information by visiting the Somerset Young Carers in Schools padlet.

Home » The Curriculum » English
English at Bishop Fox’s has changed! Due to the current government’s introduction of new GCSE courses for English Literature and Language, students will now be assessed solely by examination at KS4. To prepare for this, we offer a curriculum that is diverse and engaging, whilst providing students with the resources they need to achieve highly in KS4. Ultimately, we want our students to enjoy reading and writing in English as well as developing the skills they will need for life.
We want all of our students to passionately enjoy reading and literature. Students will study poetry, plays and novels. They will learn to analyse and infer; they will practise debate and discussion.
There is a positive correlation between regular reading and academic achievement. Reading every day is vital for improving concentration, literacy fluency, creativity and well-being, and reading for pleasure is proven to have a dramatic impact on life outcomes.
We encourage students to read daily. Our Reading Lists have been curated to represent a wide variety of fiction, both classic and modern, and non-fiction titles. Every book on the list is available at school, and students may borrow the books from the Reading Area at lunchtime. Students are recognised for books read through an Achievement point reward scheme.
To view our current reading lists, please click below:

Year 9 Reading Lists

As well as being great readers, our students are fantastic writers. We start, in Year 7, by getting the basics of grammar and sentence construction right. From there, students are encouraged to use their own creativity, flair and imagination to write in a range of styles and forms.

Media
Here at Bishop Fox’s we provide The Pearson BTEC Level 1/Level 2 Tech Award in Creative Media Production. It is for learners who want to acquire technical knowledge and technical skills through vocational contexts by applying the learned knowledge and processes related to investigating, exploring and creating media products as part of their Key Stage 4 learning.
The qualification recognises the value of learning skills, knowledge and vocational attributes to complement GCSEs. The qualification will broaden the learners experience and understanding of the varied progression options available to them.
The Award gives learners the opportunity to develop sector-specific knowledge and skills in a practical learning environment. We encourage learners to work on all areas of Media from press to moving image and radio. This course complements the learning in GCSE qualifications, such as Design and Technology, Art and Design, and Computer Science, by broadening the application of ‘design and make’ tasks, working with a media brief, and understanding and engaging different audiences through making compelling media products.

Home » The Curriculum » Health and Social Care
BTEC Health and Social Care is a work-related course. It introduces you to the employment area of Health and Social Care and provides a good basis to progress to a more advanced work-related qualification. In Year 9, students will begin with an introduction to Health and Social Care and will then move on to study Human Growth and Development. In Year 10, they will study Health and Social Care Services and Values. Students will study and prepare for an exam component in Year 11, Health and Wellbeing.
The Tech Award gives students the opportunity to develop sector-specific knowledge and skills in a practical learning environment. Lesson are based in IT rooms to allow hight quality assignments to be produced.
The main focus is on three areas, which cover:
The course is made up of three units, each of which will be assessed on a regular basis mainly through the marking of coursework including homework, presentations and role play for particular units studied. Your progress will be closely monitored to ensure that you are fully supported to achieve your potential. It is important that you meet the deadlines in order to keep up to date with the work. You will also have to sit a 3 hour exam towards the end of the course in Year 11. At the end of the three year course, you will achieve the equivalent to one GCSE, either a ‘Pass’ (grade C), a ‘Merit’ (grade B) or ‘Distinction’ (grade A).
This qualification is for students who wish to develop applied knowledge and practical skills in health and social. It is designed with both practical and theoretical elements, which will prepare students for further qualifications in Child Care, Health and Social Care, Psychology, Sociology, Early Years and Biology.
The course is made up of:
Component 1: Human Lifespan Development
Component 2: Health and Social Care Services
Component 3: Health and Wellbeing
Students will attend masterclasses, workshops with employer partners, go on external trips and visit Calway House where students work with the residents.

Home » The Curriculum » Mathematics
Our aim is for students to develop the ability to think clearly and logically and to apply these skills both in Mathematics and in other areas. Students will develop lively enquiring minds and use them creatively. We pride ourselves in helping students to be proficient in numeracy and able to deal confidently with the mathematical situations that they are likely to encounter throughout their everyday lives. We work hard with students to ensure they leave school with a good GCSE qualification in Mathematics.
At Key Stage 3 students are set by ability from the start of Year 7 based on data provided by our feeder Primary schools plus our own assessment. Current setting arrangements are based on four and three sets across half a year group. Sets are reviewed on a regular basis. The course followed includes modules based on number, algebra, shape, space, measures, data handling and ratio and proportion. Building on the foundation at KS2, great emphasis is placed on both mental and oral mathematics together with non-calculator methods of computation.
Moving to Year 9 transition year allows students to follow a three year GCSE course at either Foundation or Higher level based on their attainment at KS3.

Home » The Curriculum » Remote Learning
Remote education provision: information for parents and guardiansThis information is intended to provide clarity and transparency to students and parents / guardians about what to expect from remote education.
The remote curriculum: what is taught to students at homeA student’s first few days of being educated remotely might look different from our standard approach, while we take all necessary actions to prepare for a longer period of remote teaching.
What should my child expect from immediate remote education in the first few days?Students have immediate access to Oak National Academy lessons here for a range of subjects.
Following the first few days of remote education, will my child be taught broadly the same curriculum as they would if they were in school?We aim to teach the same curriculum remotely as we do in school wherever possible and appropriate. However, we have needed to make some adaptations in some subjects. For example, subjects which require specialist equipment and resources the lessons will be adapted to suit students learning remotely at home.
Remote teaching and study time each day
How long can I expect work set by the school to take my child each day?We expect that remote education will ensure students spend the same amount of time studying as they would if they were in school.
Accessing remote education
How will my child access any online remote education you are providing?All home learning communication and resources will be delivered through your child’s Class Charts account. If a live lesson is scheduled to take place, your child will be informed via Class Charts and then expected to log into their Microsoft Teams account.
If my child does not have digital or online access at home, how will you support them to access remote education?We recognise that some students may not have suitable online access at home. Please inform the office on 01823 289211 if you have limited access.
How will my child be taught remotely?We use a combination of the following approaches to teach students remotely depending on the context.
Oak National Academy lessons
Live lessons
Pre-recorded audio instructions embedded into PowerPoint files
Engagement and feedback
What are your expectations for my child’s engagement and the support that we as parents and carers should provide at home?Students should continue to work at home for same length of time allocated to each subject when they are in school. We suggest that students use their own school timetable to manage their day and maintain the typical structure of the school day. Students can complete the work on separate paper if they do not have their exercise book at home – we have tried to reduce the need to print various pages at home.
Use the ideas below to help create a successful home learning experience for your child:
How will you check whether my child is engaging with their work and how will I be informed if there are concerns?Tutors will monitor students engagement and contact home where concerns around the level of engagement are raised by your child’s teachers.
How will you assess my child’s work and progress?Feedback can take many forms and may not always mean extensive written comments for individual children. For example, quizzes marked automatically via Class Charts or other online platforms (e.g. Sparx or Seneca) provide both the student and teacher with important feedback. When students return from remote education we may use a short assessment to then provide whole class feedback to the group to promote progress within each subject.
Additional support for students with particular needs
How will you work with me to help my child who needs additional support from adults at home to access remote education?We recognise that some students, for example some students with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND), may not be able to access remote education without support from adults at home. We acknowledge the difficulties this may place on families, and we will work with parents and guardians to support those students. We will discuss with parents and guardians whether a printed pack is preferred over online learning and aim to support this promptly if a printed pack is selected.
Remote education for individual studentsWhere individual students need to access remote education but the majority of their peer group remains in school, how remote education is provided will likely differ from the approach for whole groups. This is due to the challenges of teaching students both at home and in school.

A broad Science education at Key Stage 3 with impressive outcomes is a useful preparation for greater choice and specialism at Key Stage 4.
At Key Stage 4 students study GCSE Science. Within the GCSE course students either follow the three separate science courses of Biology, Chemistry, Physics (known as ‘Triple Science’ worth 3 GCSE’s) or follow Combined Science worth 2 GCSE’s. All students study Biology, Chemistry and Physics at Key Stage 4.
Newly refurbished laboratories with an “enquiry based” approach to Science offer the means for every student to achieve in this area of the curriculum.

pageCache.pageTitle: Performing Arts - GCSE Dance, Drama and Music - Bishop Fox's School
pageCache.text:
Home » The Curriculum » Performing Arts – GCSE Dance, Drama and Music
The school is very proud of its outstanding tradition in the Arts.
At Key Stage 3 students are taught Music, Dance and Drama as separate subjects and all three of these subjects are highly successful options in Key Stage 4 together with BTEC Performing Arts.
Students regularly participate in local and national competitions and performances and peripatetic music lessons are available to practicing musicians.
Outstanding school performances are held each year with the School Carol Concert, Dance Show, Evening of Excellence in Music and several productions which include whole school productions and GCSE Drama Exam performances. Key Stage 3 productions have recently included Matilda, Alice in Wonderland, DNA and Dr Kerczaks Example.
Students regularly partake in workshops with national and international dance and theatre companies including Gecko Theatre, Frantic Assembly, The Paperbirds and Swindon Dance Company.
Performing Arts Ties are awarded to students for excellence in the Arts.

pageCache.pageTitle: SEND and Inclusion at Bishop Fox’s - Bishop Fox's School
pageCache.text:
Home » About the School » SEND and Inclusion at Bishop Fox’s
Welcome to SEND and Inclusion at Bishop Fox’s School.
At Bishop Fox’s, we believe that inclusion begins with knowing our learners well, maintaining high expectations and identifying and removing barriers to learning and participation. We are committed to ensuring that students with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND) are known, valued, included and supported to achieve ambitious outcomes.
Our approach begins in the classroom. High-quality, inclusive and adaptive teaching is the foundation of our provision, with teachers using their knowledge of learners, assessment and information about individual needs to anticipate barriers and make appropriate adaptations and reasonable adjustments.
Where students require support that is different from or additional to our universal provision, we use the graduated approach – Assess, Plan, Do, Review – to understand need, plan appropriate provision and evaluate its impact. This may include targeted intervention, specialist advice or more individualised support, according to the needs of the learner.
Students with identified SEND have an Inclusive Learning Plan (ILP) where appropriate, which captures their individual strengths, needs, voice and the personalised strategies and reasonable adjustments that support them. Our focus is not simply on providing support, but on developing participation, confidence and independence.
Working together Inclusion is a shared responsibility. Our SEND and Inclusion Team works closely with students, families, teachers, pastoral colleagues and external professionals to ensure that needs are understood and that support is coordinated effectively. We place particular importance on early identification and transition, using information from primary schools, families, students, assessment and our own observations to understand learners as early as possible and respond to emerging barriers.
Our wider inclusion provision provides targeted support for students experiencing particular barriers to learning, regulation, attendance and engagement. Provision is needs-led, planned and reviewed, with the aim of supporting successful participation in education and positive outcomes.
Our SEND and Inclusion provision is led by Ms A Trigg, Assistant Headteacher – SEND and Inclusion, supported by our SEND team and experienced Learning Support Assistants, who work alongside teachers to promote access, participation and increasing independence.
For further information about our SEND provision, graduated approach, accessibility and support available at Bishop Fox’s, please explore the information and documents available on these pages.
